notes:
Quick CRM snapshot: Returnspring is a mid-market SaaS platform (merchant-facing returns & label orchestration). Heavy seasonality (Black Friday / Cyber week: observed 8-12x traffic spike). Primary product is agent UI used by merchant support + automated bot fallbacks. Evaluating Redwood Hosted API first (fast time-to-value) with view to Dedicated for predictable peak capacity. 

Primary ask from product/infra: p95 end-to-end chat response (streaming to UI + tool calls to carrier APIs) must stay <= 700ms under normal load, <= 1s acceptable with graceful degradation during peak; p95 token-to-client stream latency target = 250-350ms. Emphasis on streaming reliability, tool calling (create_label, cancel_rma, carrier_lookup), and deterministic fallbacks to smaller model variants when GPU constrained.

Security & compliance: SOC2 in place but legal wants explicit data residency guarantees for EU merchants; SSO via SAML already in use. Need audit-log export into their SIEM and customer-managed KMS support for Protected PII in shipment manifests.

Commercial: Pricing sensitivity around monthly burst credit vs. Dedicated monthly commit. CFO asked for TCO comparison for 3 capacity profiles (steady, seasonal, bursty). They pushed back on per-token variability; want clearer unit economics from Redwood Optimize recommendations.

Decision timeline: internal Readout 2026-05-12 (executive + infra). Favored Redwood if Hosted POC meets latency SLOs and SE sizing shows Dedicated can be cost-predictable for peak week(s).
